title: feat: sync Cloudflare traffic for every pollinations.ai host to Tinybird daily
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The pollinations.ai zone (Free plan) reports 31 days of per-request detail and a 30-day maximum query range. This syncs it daily into Tinybird so the history is kept, for every `*.pollinations.ai` host.

**What we get** (per UTC day)
- `page_views`: pollinations.ai, www and enter by page, HTTP status, country, device and browser
- `host_views`: every host with traffic that day (about 46: API, apps, docs, blog, MCP, media, previews, staging) by HTTP status, content type (page, JSON, image), country, device and browser. Gives country and device for API traffic, which our own request logs don't record
- Verified bots labelled (crawlers, link previews, SEO tools) and HTTP status stored, so bots, redirects, errors and challenges can be separated from real page loads

**What we don't get**: referrers (not on the Free plan), who the visitor is, exact counts (Cloudflare samples busy days). Each row is the unchanged response of the fields requested here; fields not requested cannot be recovered later.

**Privacy**
- Real clients only; our Workers' own outgoing calls are left out
- Paths only for our own page routes. People type prompts into URLs, so `host_views` has no path at all
- No IP or user-agent string is requested

**Changes**
- `cloudflare_traffic_raw`: one response per dataset, day and host (`dataset, date, host, fetched_at, body`), ~47 rows / ~9 MB per day. Append-only: a rerun adds the same day and host again, and consumers must select the latest `fetched_at` per `(dataset, date, host)` before aggregating (stated in the datasource description). No pipe or other consumer reads it yet
- `data-sync-cloudflare-traffic-tinybird.yml`: daily at 05:15 UTC for the previous day (~80 s); a manual run takes `days` (1–7) for a missed run; 20-minute timeout
- `operations/cloudflare/sync-traffic-to-tinybird.mjs`: queries paced under Cloudflare's 300-per-5-minutes limit; a host with more groups than one query returns (10,000) is fetched as two halves by country code and stored a

gist.headline: A longer memory for traffic
gist.blurb: Cloudflare’s traffic history now gets a daily shelf in Tinybird. Polli can count the visitors without collecting their prompts.
gist.summary: A daily 05:15 UTC sync saves the previous day’s Cloudflare traffic for every pollinations.ai host to Tinybird, preserving host, country, device, browser, status and bot breakdowns beyond Cloudflare’s 31-day detail window.
gist.impact: Maintainers can examine longer-term traffic across roughly 46 hosts, including API geography and device data, without storing IPs, user-agent strings or prompt-bearing paths.
gist.visual_concept: Polli tends a growing archive of daily traffic records in a cozy server garden. Small signposts for different hosts and simple country, device and bot icons show what the records contain; closed envelopes represent prompt paths deliberately left out.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art server garden, Polli files yesterday’s traffic record on a growing shelf beside a lime green (#ecf874) CRT terminal, while tiny flowers mark different hosts and sealed envelopes stay outside the archive. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears a tiny archivist’s visor and shares the scene with chunky retro sprites against a soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes; nostalgic but beautiful, emotionally warm.
